newsitem.title: TURKEY: Barzani meets Turkey's Ciller before US talks.
newsitem.headline: Barzani meets Turkey's Ciller before US talks.

text.p: Baghdad-backed Iraqi Kurdish leader Massoud Barzani met Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller before talks on Wednesday with U.S. officials who want him to sever ties to Iraqi President Saddam Hussein, diplomats said.
"It was a very good meeting between Mr Barzani and Madam Ciller," Sami Abderrahman, a senior Barzani aide, told reporters after the meeting.

A Western diplomatic source said Barzani would meet Robert Pelletreau, U.S. assistant secretary of state for near eastern affairs, in the afternoon -- his first talks with Washington since seizing control of northern Iraq from a rival Kurdish militia.
The source said British diplomats would also attend the meeting, which State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns had orginally said would be held on Thursday.
Washington would like Barzani to halt cooperation with Saddam so it could pick up the pieces of its shattered policy on north Iraq.
"The Americans will want assurances that Saddam will not take over northern Iraq," the source said. He said the venue for the meeting was as of yet unclear.
Barzani's Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), backed by Iraqi troops and tanks, captured the Kurdish city of Arbil from a rival militia last month, prompting U.S. missile strikes on southern Iraq.
Washington has pulled back military, aid and intelligence operations from Iraq, fearing Barzani's new ties to the central government in Baghdad would put U.S. personnel and their local staff at risk.
